traits.flower_symmetry.note: FNA Xyris (read 2026-10-17): three equal, clawed petals over unequal sepals, so the showy corolla is radial in Xyris (>250 spp, most of the family). Zygomorphic flowers belong to the small genera, and the uneven sepals keep it at sometimes.

traits.inflorescence.note: FNA Xyris (read 2026-10-17): flowers single in the axils of tight bracts on a terminal spike atop a scape. Xyris (>250 spp) dominates the family; the short cone-like spike is sometimes called a head, so head stays as sometimes.

traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Xyridaceae: leaves alternate; leaves simple; veins parallel; blades linear; leaf rosettes basal; plants hermaphrodite; ovary superior; stems herbaceous; flowers in spikes or in heads; flowers actinomorphic or zygomorphic; perianth sepals and petals; fruit capsule; parts of each whorl 3; stamens 3; carpels 3. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.zygomorphy.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Xyridaceae: its irregular flowers are of no named kind (pea flower, two lips, orchid lip), read from the coded corolla symmetry (spec-rework/b1/delta): zygomorphy other. Its flowers are not mostly zygomorphic, so a plant of it states its own symmetry; one that is zygomorphic draws this kind, and one stating none is drawn regular.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: FNA Xyris (read 2026-10-17): over 250 spp, leaves two-ranked and equitant (folded astride one another). Xyris holds the large majority of the family's species; spirally leaved members are in the small South American genera (Abolboda and allies). Re-ranks the earlier value, from plant-systematics-simpson, whose top states were tied.

traits.bract_form.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 271, family Xyridaceae: bract form scale; imbricate, hardened bracts each subtending a flower; read as "scale".

traits.flowering_position.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 271, family Xyridaceae: flowering position terminal; read as "terminal".

traits.life_span.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 269, family Xyridaceae: life span perennial or annual; read as {"annual": "often", "perennial": "often"}.

traits.perennation.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Xyridaceae: how its perennial herbs last from year to year (character 25), coded usually a rhizome. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 25 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.
